title: threat modeling secure design audit logging and incident response
concepts: Threat modeling starts with assets, trust boundaries, data flows, attacker goals, and plausible abuse cases. Controls follow from risk, not from an undifferentiated checklist.
Secure design applies least privilege, defense in depth, fail-safe defaults, explicit trust boundaries, and separation of duties throughout architecture and deployment.

Security logs support detection and investigation but must exclude passwords, access tokens, session identifiers, and other secrets. Events need consistent context, access control, integrity protection, and retention.
Incident response prepares teams to detect, contain, eradicate, recover, preserve evidence, and improve controls. Roles, escalation, and recovery responsibilities are defined before an incident.

inventory.title: Assets, trust boundaries, threat identification, and risk treatment
Security events, protected logs, response lifecycle, and recovery

items: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3 integrates incident response into broader cybersecurity risk management and supersedes Rev. 2 as the current revision.

scopeExclusions: Detailed attack mitigations are covered in t05-001 through t05-009.
Legal breach notification duties vary by jurisdiction and are not summarized as legal advice.
Provider-specific SIEM query languages and incident tooling are outside scope.
